Medeba
MED-eh-buh
proper noun
From the Hebrew, commonly understood as “waters of quiet” or “water of rest”.

📖 Biblical Definition

Medeba was both a city and the broad upland plain bearing its name, lying in the Transjordan country taken from Sihon. When the inheritance east of the Jordan was divided, the plain of Medeba fell within the portion of the tribe of Reuben, reaching from Aroer on the Arnon and including the table-land round about. It was thus part of the eastern allotment of Israel, a region of pasture and high ground well suited to the cattle of which Reuben and Gad had much. In the days of David, the children of Ammon and the hired Syrians arrayed themselves for battle before Medeba, and there Joab and Abishai routed them. Yet, like its neighbor cities, Medeba did not remain securely in Israel’s hand; it reverted to Moab and appears in Isaiah’s oracle, where Moab howls over Nebo and over Medeba, every head bald and every beard cut in mourning. The city’s history mirrors the wider Transjordan story: granted to Israel by the LORD’s victories, lost through declension, and made at last a theatre of judgment upon Moab. Medeba reminds us that the providence of God governs the bounds of every people’s habitation. He sets the tribes in their inheritance, and He removes them; the rest promised in the name “waters of quiet” is found at last not in any plain but in Christ.

📜 Webster 1828 Definition

A city and upland plain east of the Jordan, allotted to Reuben, and named among the places of Moab’s mourning in the prophets.

MEDEBA, a city and broad table-land east of the Jordan in the territory taken from Sihon.

Assigned with its plain to the tribe of Reuben in the Transjordan allotment (Jos 13:16).

The plain of Medeba named as part of Reuben’s border (Jos 13:9).

Scene of battle when Ammon and Syria fought David’s armies (1Ch 19:7).

A place of Moabite mourning in Isaiah’s oracle (Isa 15:2).

📖 Key Scripture

Jos 13:9 — "From Aroer, that is upon the bank of the river Arnon, and the city that is in the midst of the river, and all the plain of Medeba unto Dibon;"

Jos 13:16 — "And their coast was from Aroer, that is on the bank of the river Arnon, and the city that is in the midst of the river, and all the plain by Medeba;"

Isa 15:2 — "He is gone up to Bajith, and to Dibon, the high places, to weep: Moab shall howl over Nebo, and over Medeba: on all their heads shall be baldness, and every beard cut off."

1Ch 19:7 — "So they hired thirty and two thousand chariots, and the king of Maachah and his people; who came and pitched before Medeba. And the children of Ammon gathered themselves together from their cities, and came to battle."

⚠️ Modern Corruption

The lesson to recover is that God appoints and removes the inheritance of peoples, and true rest is found only in Christ.

expand to see more

This entry faces no significant postmodern redefinition. Medeba, whose name breathes of “waters of quiet,” teaches that the LORD “hath determined the times before appointed, and the bounds of their habitation.” The plain given to Reuben was a real and good inheritance, yet earthly rest proved fleeting; the city passed to Moab and became a place of weeping. No portion of ground secures lasting peace.

The believer reads in Medeba a parable of the soul’s true rest. The quiet that its name promised is found not in any allotment of land but in Him who said, “Come unto me, all ye that labour and are heavy laden, and I will give you rest.” Earthly inheritances pass from hand to hand under the discipline of God; the inheritance of the saints is incorruptible, reserved in heaven.

🔗 Greek & Hebrew Roots

The name is generally read as “waters of quiet” or “water of rest,” joining the word for water with a root for stillness.

expand to see more

Medeba — from Hebrew, “waters of quiet” or “water of rest.”

The first element me reflects mayim, “waters.”

The latter element is linked to a root for quietness or gentle flow.

Fitting a well-watered upland plain amid the eastern table-land.

Used both of the city and of the broad plain that bore its name (Jos 13:9).

Usage

"The plain of Medeba was reckoned to Reuben among the eastern inheritances."

"Before Medeba the hired Syrians pitched their tents against the men of David."

"Isaiah heard Moab howl over Medeba, every head shaved in bitter mourning."
